summary: Requested edit applied and verified (compile + preflight clean). Remaining whole-design critique is advisory and targets content this turn did not modify.

diagnostics.message: The hero image is a generic teal-to-blue gradient with a soft white glow — reads as a placeholder or abstract wallpaper, not a credible case-study photo. Fails imagery Relevance and Placeholder-vs-Real.
diagnostics.hint: Replace the hero asset with a real, on-brief editorial photograph (e.g. a calm clinic front desk / triage moment). Regenerate via asset(action="generate_image") with a concrete subject + editorial photograph medium + clean negative space; do not use an abstract gradient.

diagnostics.message: Huge dead vertical band between the headline and the body line, and a second dead band below the body to the canvas bottom. Gaps inside the text stack are irregular (kicker→headline tight, headline→body enormous), so the copy reads as three stranded strips rather than one anchored block.
diagnostics.hint: On band, tighten and equalize the stack with g($space.stack.default) and let the band hug its content, then wrap it in a fill-height main so it centers vertically under the image — no manufactured spacer gaps.

diagnostics.message: The eyebrow, headline, and body text run to the very left edge of the 1080pt canvas with zero outer margin, while the image sits with a small top/side inset. The alignment spine is inconsistent and the text feels bled off the page.
diagnostics.hint: Add symmetric outer padding to the canvas (e.g. pad(80) on the root auto_layout) so all children — hero image and text band — share the same left/right margin and align to one spine.

diagnostics.message: The image occupies ~55% of the canvas top; the bottom ~45% contains three thin text lines with two huge empty bands. Whitespace reads as dead space, not margin around a coherent block.
diagnostics.hint: Either reduce the image height and center the copy in a fill-height main region below it, or move to a full-bleed hero + scrim + text idiom so the message sits over the image with proper distribution.

diagnostics.message: Headline size is modest for a 1080×1350 poster; combined with the visual weight of the huge image above, the headline does not clearly dominate the composition.
diagnostics.hint: Step the headline size up with font_size($type.size.6xl) or 7xl on #headline while keeping style($type.headline).
